metaData.originalTitle: Agent Harness 解析：智能体架构深度拆解
metaData.title: Agent Harness Analysis: A Deep Dive into Agent Architecture
metaData.oneSentenceSummary: This article provides an in-depth analysis of the Agent Harness concept, defining it as the complete software infrastructure surrounding an LLM, and systematically explains its 12 core components, operational loop, and implementation approaches in mainstream frameworks.
metaData.summary: Starting from common challenges encountered in production-grade AI Agent development, the article formally introduces the concept of Agent Harness—the complete software infrastructure wrapping an LLM, including orchestration loops, tools, memory, and context management. It points out that while model capabilities are important, it is the surrounding Harness that truly determines the performance of production-grade Agents. The author breaks down the 12 core components of a production-grade Harness, such as orchestration loops, tools, memory, context management, prompt construction, output parsing, state management, error handling, guardrails and safety, validation loops, and sub-Agent orchestration. The article also demonstrates the actual operation of the Harness loop through a step-by-step walkthrough and compares the implementation patterns of mainstream frameworks including Anthropic, OpenAI, LangGraph, CrewAI, and AutoGen. Finally, it summarizes seven key decisions every Harness faces and emphasizes the importance of Harness as a core product differentiator.

mainPoints.point: Agent Harness is the complete software infrastructure wrapping an LLM and is the key factor determining production-grade Agent performance.
mainPoints.explanation: Using a case study of LangChain on TerminalBench, the article demonstrates that changing only the Harness without modifying model weights can significantly improve Agent performance, proving that Harness is an engineering area more worthy of attention than the model itself.

mainPoints.point: A production-grade Harness includes 12 core components, such as orchestration loops, tools, memory, and context management.
mainPoints.explanation: The article breaks down these components in detail and points out that context management is where many Agents silently fail, requiring strategies such as compression, observation masking, and just-in-time retrieval to combat context decay.

mainPoints.point: Mainstream frameworks (Anthropic, OpenAI, LangGraph, etc.) implement the Harness pattern in different ways.
mainPoints.explanation: Anthropic adopts a thin Harness and dumb loop, delegating intelligence to the model; OpenAI's SDK is code-first; LangGraph models the Harness as an explicit state graph. These different implementations reflect varying trade-offs in Harness thickness.

mainPoints.point: Harness design faces seven key decisions, including single/multi-Agent, ReAct/plan-execute, and Harness thickness.
mainPoints.explanation: The article recommends prioritizing single-Agent solutions and notes that as model capabilities improve, the Harness should trend thinner but will not disappear. Harness design is central to product differentiation.

keyQuotes: If you are not the model itself, you are the harness.

A bare LLM is a CPU with no memory, no hard drive, and no I/O. The context window is RAM—fast but limited; external databases are the hard drive—large but slow; tool integration is device drivers; the Harness is the operating system.
Next time your agent fails, don't blame the model—look at the Harness.
Two products using the same model can achieve vastly different performance based solely on Harness design.
